blocks.text: הָעוֹלָמִים אֲדוֹן כָּל־הַבְּרִיּוֹת אֱלוֹהַּ כָּל־הַנְּפָשׁוֹת: הַיּוֹשֵׁב בְּמֶרְחֲבֵי מָרוֹם הַשּׁוֹכֵן בִּשְׁמֵי שְׁמֵי קֶדֶם: קְדֻשָּׁתוֹ עַל הַחַיּוֹת וּקְדֻשָּׁתוֹ עַל כִּסֵּא הַכָּבוֹד: וּבְכֵן יִתְקַדַּשׁ שִׁמְךָ בָּנוּ יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ לְעֵינֵי כָּל־חָי: וְנֹאמַר לְפָנָיו שִׁיר חָדָשׁ כַּכָּתוּב: שִׁירוּ לֵאלֹהִים זַמְּרוּ שְׁמוֹ סֹלּוּ לָרוֹכֵב בָּעֲרָבוֹת בְּיָהּ שְׁמוֹ וְעִלְזוּ לְפָנָיו: וְנִרְאֵהוּ עַיִן בְּעַיִן בְּשׁוּבוֹ אֶל נָוֵהוּ כַּכָּתוּב: כִּי עַיִן בְּעַיִן יִרְאוּ בְּשׁוּב יְיָ צִיּוֹן: וְנֶאֱמַר וְנִגְלָה כְּבוֹד יְיָ וְרָאוּ כָל־בָּשָׂר יַחְדָּו כִּי פִּי יְיָ דִּבֵּר:

blocks.text: אַב הָרַחֲמִים הוּא יְרַחֵם עַם עֲמוּסִים וְיִזְכּוֹר בְּרִית אֵתָנִים וְיַצִּיל נַפְשׁוֹתֵינוּ מִן הַשָּׁעוֹת הָרָעוֹת וְיִגְעַר בְּיֵצֶר הָרַע מִן הַנְּשׂוּאִים וְיָחֹן אוֹתָנוּ לִפְלֵיטַת עוֹלָמִים וִימַלֵּא מִשְׁאֲלוֹתֵינוּ בְּמִדָּה טוֹבָה יְשׁוּעָה וְרַחֲמִים:
uncertainties: אֵתָנִים: the vowel under the alef looks like tsere.
וְיָחֹן: it is unclear whether the holam is written defectively or a vav is present. It reads as defective (no vav).

blocks.text: The Torah scroll is laid on the reading desk and unrolled. The reader then calls upon the Cohen, saying:

וְיַעֲזוֹר וְיָגֵן וְיוֹשִׁיעַ לְכָל הַחוֹסִים בּוֹ וְנֹאמַר אָמֵן: הַכֹּל הָבוּ גֹדֶל לֵאלֹהֵינוּ וּתְנוּ כָבוֹד לַתּוֹרָה כֹּהֵן קְרָב. יַעֲמוֹד (פלוני בר פלוני הכהן): בָּרוּךְ שֶׁנָּתַן תּוֹרָה לְעַמּוֹ יִשְׂרָאֵל בִּקְדֻשָּׁתוֹ: תּוֹרַת יְיָ תְּמִימָה מְשִׁיבַת נָפֶשׁ עֵדוּת יְיָ נֶאֱמָנָה מַחְכִּימַת פֶּתִי: פִּקּוּדֵי יְיָ יְשָׁרִים מְשַׂמְּחֵי לֵב מִצְוַת יְיָ בָּרָה מְאִירַת עֵינָיִם: יְיָ עֹז לְעַמּוֹ יִתֵּן יְיָ יְבָרֵךְ אֶת עַמּוֹ בַשָּׁלוֹם: הָאֵל תָּמִים דַּרְכּוֹ אִמְרַת יְיָ צְרוּפָה מָגֵן הוּא לְכֹל הַחֹסִים בּוֹ:
uncertainties: In the first line, the vowel under the kaf of לְכָל is unclear. It could be qamats or holam (לְכֹל). The last line clearly reads לְכֹל הַחֹסִים.
In גֹדֶל the gimel seems to have no dagesh.
The parenthetical (פלוני בר פלוני הכהן) is printed small and unpointed.
The sentence הַכֹּל הָבוּ ... קְרָב ends with a period, not a sof pasuq colon.
The word is spelled הַחוֹסִים (plene) in the first line and הַחֹסִים (defective) in the last line, as printed.

blocks.text: וְאַתֶּם הַדְּבֵקִים בַּייָ אֱלֹהֵיכֶם חַיִּים כֻּלְּכֶם הַיּוֹם:

blocks.text: 72 Prayer while the Scrolls of the Torah are taken out of the Ark 72

of all souls, who dwells in the infinite heights, and resides in the primaeval heavens, His holiness is above the Hayoth, His holiness is above the glorious throne. And thus may Thy Name be sanctified among us, O Lord our God, before the eyes of all the living; and let us sing before Him a new song, as it is written: ‘Sing to God, sing praise of His Name. Exalt Him who rides upon the clouds, Yah is His Name, and rejoice before Him. We shall see Him eye to eye when He returns to His dwelling as it is written: eye to eye shall they behold when the Lord returns to Zion. And it was said: ‘And the glory of the Lord shall be revealed and all flesh together shall see, for the mouth of the Lord has spoken’.
uncertainties: This paragraph starts on the previous page, mid-sentence.
The opening quotation mark before ‘Sing to God...’ has no matching closing mark, as printed.
There is a small speck after 'eye' in 'eye to eye shall they behold'. It is probably a print artifact and not punctuation.

blocks.text: The father of mercy will have mercy upon the people borne by Him and remember the covenant with the eternal ones (forefathers) and deliver our souls from evil hours and rebuke the evil inclination from those whom He has lifted up and favour us for eternal refuge and fulfil our prayers with a full measure of salvation and compassion.
The Torah scroll is laid on the reading desk and unrolled. The reader then calls upon the Cohen, saying:

And He will help, protect and save all who shelter with Him, and let us say: Amen. Let all of you ascribe greatness to our God and honour the Torah, let the Cohen approach. Let there arise . . . Blessed be He, who in His holiness has given the Torah to His people Israel. The Torah of the Lord is flawless, refreshing the soul; the testimony of the Lord is faithful, making the simple wise. The precepts of the Lord are upright, causing the heart to rejoice, the commandment of the Lord is clear, giving light to the eyes. The Lord gives strength to His people, the Lord blesses His people with peace: God’s way is perfect, the Lord’s word is pure, a shield is He for all who shelter with Him.
uncertainties: Two words were hyphenated across line breaks and have been joined: 'ap-proach' and 'command-ment'.
